failures.title: Ford KNBA Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Coolant System Leaks - Water Pump and Thermostat Housing - 2019+ units
items.whatHappens: The KNBA's coolant system is critical to both engine operation and hybrid battery thermal management. The water pump and thermostat housing are plastic-composite units prone to cracking or seal degradation over time. Symptoms include unexplained coolant loss, overheating warnings, and in severe cases, the hybrid system entering limp mode to protect the battery. If ignored, overheating can lead to head gasket failure or warped cylinder head components.
items.repairVsReplace: Water pump and thermostat housing replacement is a routine repair if caught early. However, if overheating has caused head gasket damage or cylinder head warping, a full reconditioned KNBA becomes the more reliable long-term solution. Read our full head gasket failure guide.

items.title: Throttle Body Carbon Buildup - 2019+ units
items.whatHappens: As an Atkinson-cycle engine, the KNBA operates with specific intake manifold pressures that can promote carbon deposition on the throttle body and intake valves over time. Symptoms include rough idle, hesitation on acceleration, and occasional engine management light illumination. The hybrid system's frequent engine start-stop cycles can exacerbate carbon buildup compared to conventional continuous-running engines.
items.repairVsReplace: Throttle body cleaning or replacement is a straightforward repair. However, if carbon buildup has caused prolonged misfires or catalytic converter damage, engine replacement may be necessary. Read our full throttle body failure guide.

failures.goodYearsLine: The KNBA is generally considered a robust hybrid powertrain when maintained with strict coolant system inspections and hybrid battery health checks. The Atkinson-cycle design is inherently simpler than turbocharged engines, with fewer high-stress components .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the KNBA
variants.intro: The KNBA engine code is stamped directly onto the engine block, typically located on a machined pad near the bellhousing or on the cylinder head cover. It is also clearly listed on your vehicle's V5C registration document under "Engine Capacity/Code" and can be independently verified via a VIN decode.

relatives.description: The earlier hybrid powertrain used in pre-2019 Mondeo Hybrid models, offering lower displacement and less refined hybrid integration compared to the KNBA's 2.5L architecture.

M8DA (1.5L EcoBoost) - A completely different engine family (turbocharged petrol vs. naturally aspirated hybrid), but frequently confused by owners due to similar Ford model applications. The M8DA has its own distinct coolant intrusion issues.

The conventional turbocharged petrol alternative to the KNBA hybrid, offering higher performance but without the efficiency benefits. Owners considering engine replacement should verify whether their vehicle is hybrid or conventional before ordering.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement KNBA - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used KNBA is only advisable if the donor vehicle's hybrid battery health is verified and the eCVT transmission has a documented service history. Given the integrated nature of the hybrid system, a used engine without battery and transmission verification carries significant risk of inheriting latent faults. Explore used Ford engines.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A proper reconditioned KNBA is the most recommended path for most owners. A reputable rebuild will address the core weaknesses by replacing the water pump and thermostat housing, cleaning or renewing the throttle body, and verifying all coolant system seals. This resolves the dominant failure patterns while keeping costs well below a full custom rebuild. Explore reconditioned Ford engines.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified if the original KNBA suffered catastrophic failure due to severe overheating or hybrid system electrical faults that damaged the engine internals. An upgraded rebuild should include a revised water pump design, enhanced thermostat housing, and updated ECU mapping to address known carbon buildup tendencies. Explore rebuilt Ford engines.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Our network of vetted UK hybrid specialists can supply the KNBA unit and handle the complete installation, including hybrid system integration, eCVT calibration, and high-voltage battery health verification, backed by a minimum 12-month warranty. Learn more about supply & fit.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The KNBA is typically found in Ford Mondeo, S-MAX, and Galaxy Hybrid models valued between £8,000 and £18,000 depending on age, mileage, and specification. If your vehicle is at the lower end of this spectrum (e.g., an early 2019 model with over 100,000 miles), a £2,500+ reconditioned engine replacement may approach 40-50% of the car's current market value. In these specific scenarios, it is financially prudent to evaluate the vehicle's scrap or part-exchange value first, particularly if the hybrid battery also requires attention. However, for well-maintained, higher-value examples, investing in a properly reconditioned KNBA remains a cost-effective alternative to vehicle replacement.

items.question: What is the most common problem with the Ford KNBA 2.5 Hybrid?
items.answer: The dominant failures are coolant system leaks from the water pump and thermostat housing, and throttle body carbon buildup, typically emerging between 60,000 and 120,000 miles. Symptoms include unexplained coolant loss, rough idle, and hybrid system limp mode. Ignoring coolant leaks leads to overheating and potential head gasket failure.

items.answer: The KNBA 2.5L Duratec Hybrid was fitted to the Ford Mondeo (Mk5 facelift), S-MAX (Mk2 facelift), and Galaxy (Mk3 facelift) from 2019 onwards. It serves as Ford's primary hybrid powertrain for large MPVs and saloons. Always verify your specific chassis via registration lookup before ordering.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned KNBA engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned KNBA is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the integrated nature of the hybrid system and the risk of inheriting latent coolant or throttle body faults. A proper recon includes renewed water pump, thermostat housing, and throttle body service. A used unit without hybrid battery verification may pass hidden faults to your car.
bullets: A proper recon includes renewed water pump, thermostat housing, and throttle body service.
A used unit without hybrid battery verification may pass hidden faults to your car.

items.question: How do I know if my car has the KNBA engine code?
items.answer: The KNBA code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically near the bellhousing or on the cylinder head cover, and is listed on your V5C document. It is frequently confused with the earlier 2.0L Duratec HE Hybrid or conventional 2.0L EcoBoost engines like R9DA. Fitting the wrong engine causes complete hybrid system incompatibility.
